facts.text: Albany earned its name when three brothers from New York arrived in July 1813 and christened the settlement after Albany, New York.
The town’s glass legacy lives on at the Albany Glass Museum, where visitors can see ornate pieces that once defined the region’s art‑glass industry.
The New Albany High School radio station, WNAS‑FM, began broadcasting in 1949, making it the oldest continuously operating high‑school station in the nation.
During the late 1960s, Slate Run Elementary pioneered student‑produced closed‑circuit television, becoming one of the first schools in the country to offer such a program.
Albany sits on the Ohio River opposite Louisville, Kentucky, and its riverfront once hosted a bustling steamboat industry that fueled the town’s early growth.
